defaultGuidance.summary: Country-specific mortgage rules have not yet been verified against an official source for this market. Use this as a general repayment estimate only; confirm the applicable lending, tax, fee and eligibility rules with the local regulator and lender.
rules: No country-specific down-payment, loan-to-value, affordability, tax or fee rule is asserted here.
Enter the interest rate, term, payment frequency and compounding method from your lender's written offer.
Local property taxes, transfer duties, insurance, subsidies, eligibility and lender charges are not automatically included.

regionalFramework.summary: EU mortgage-credit rules provide a shared consumer-protection framework, including lender creditworthiness assessment and standardized pre-contractual information. National law, taxes, property costs and competent authorities still differ by Member State.
rules: EU-level rules require lenders to assess creditworthiness before granting mortgage credit; national law and supervisory practice add country-specific requirements.
Use the linked European Banking Authority directory to identify the national consumer-protection authority for this Member State.
This page does not calculate local transfer taxes, registration fees, national subsidies, affordability thresholds or lender-specific terms.
sources: European Commission: Mortgage loans and credit in the EU
European Banking Authority: National consumer-protection authorities

IN.summary: Reserve Bank of India guidance highlights fixed versus floating rates, benchmark resets, APR and lender fees. Housing-finance-company LTV ceilings are a separate regulated category and should not be treated as a universal down-payment rule for every lender.
rules: Ask the lender whether the rate is fixed or floating, which benchmark applies, when it resets and how EMI or loan tenure can change.
Compare APR and all fees, including processing, legal, valuation, documentation, switching and prepayment charges; stamp duty and registration are separate purchase costs.

RBI's 2025 HFC directions set maximum LTV bands for housing finance companies: up to 90% for loans up to ₹30 lakh, 80% above ₹30 lakh to ₹75 lakh, and 75% above ₹75 lakh. These HFC-specific ceilings are not a promise of approval or a universal rule for every lender.
sources: RBI: Floating-rate EMI loan reset FAQ (2025)
RBI: Housing Finance Company Master Directions (2025)

US.summary: US federal consumer rules include an ability-to-repay assessment for most residential mortgages and standardized Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure documents. State, loan-program and lender terms can add differences.
rules: Most lenders must make a reasonable, good-faith ability-to-repay determination using documented borrower financial information.
The Loan Estimate summarizes expected loan terms and costs; the Closing Disclosure sets out final terms and closing costs and is generally due at least three business days before closing.
This calculator does not estimate credit approval, mortgage insurance, property tax, homeowners association dues or state-specific closing costs unless you enter applicable amounts.
sources: CFPB: Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure documents
US Code: Minimum standards for residential mortgage loans

CA.summary: Federally regulated Canadian lenders must provide clear mortgage disclosures and an information box. The Canadian fixed-rate mortgage convention commonly uses nominal annual interest compounded semi-annually; match the actual agreement.
rules: Review the mortgage information box and disclosure statement for rate, payment, term, fees and prepayment conditions.
The calculator preselects semi-annual compounding for Canada, but you should confirm the exact convention and payment schedule in the lender's contract.
Provincial rules, land-transfer taxes, insurance premiums and lender qualification policies are not automatically calculated.
sources: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada: Mortgage rights and disclosures

GB.summary: UK deposit sizes and affordability depend on lender and product. MoneyHelper describes 5%–20% as a typical deposit range, not a statutory minimum or guarantee; lenders apply their own affordability criteria.
rules: MoneyHelper says a deposit is typically around 5%–20% of the purchase price; a larger deposit may improve available rates, but lender terms vary.
Lenders assess affordability and individual circumstances; the calculator does not determine mortgage eligibility.
Stamp Duty Land Tax in England and Northern Ireland, Land Transaction Tax in Wales and Land and Buildings Transaction Tax in Scotland have different rules and are not calculated here.
sources: MoneyHelper: How much can you afford to borrow?
MoneyHelper: Mortgage fees and buying costs

AU.summary: Australian home-loan comparisons use a comparison rate that combines the interest rate with most fees and charges, but excludes some government charges and conditional fees. Repayment frequency and loan features matter.
rules: Compare the advertised interest rate with the comparison rate; the comparison rate includes most fees but not every government or conditional charge.
Check offset/redraw features, extra repayment limits, ongoing fees, fixed-rate expiry and break costs in the lender's Key Facts Sheet and contract.
The calculator does not apply state or territory transfer duty, lenders mortgage insurance or lender-specific serviceability rules.
sources: ASIC: National Credit Code and comparison-rate explanation

AE.summary: The Central Bank of the UAE sets borrower-based mortgage measures including loan-to-value limits, debt-burden ratio caps, maximum finance amounts and loan terms. LTV treatment differs by borrower category and property purpose/value.
rules: UAE LTV limits vary by UAE national versus expatriate, first owner-occupied home versus subsequent/investment property, and property value. Off-plan property has separate treatment.
The Central Bank framework also includes debt-burden and maximum-loan-term controls; the calculator does not decide eligibility or apply a bank's full affordability assessment.
Confirm the current CBUAE rule and your bank's terms before using any down-payment figure. No universal UAE deposit percentage is assumed here.
sources: Central Bank of the UAE: Borrower-based mortgage measures
CBUAE Rulebook: Regulations regarding mortgage loans

NZ.summary: New Zealand's Reserve Bank sets high-LVR lending speed limits for banks, not a guaranteed deposit requirement for each borrower. Banks still apply their own lending criteria.
rules: Current settings allow up to 25% of new owner-occupier lending to be above 80% LVR and up to 10% of investor lending to be above 70% LVR; these are portfolio speed limits, not individual approval entitlements.
The Reserve Bank reviews settings over time. Check the current RBNZ rules and the lender's own affordability assessment.
The calculator does not apply DTI restrictions, first-home loan exemptions or lender-specific criteria.
sources: Reserve Bank of New Zealand: Loan-to-value ratio restrictions

SG.summary: Singapore home purchases can incur Buyer's Stamp Duty based on the higher of purchase price or market value. Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty depends on buyer profile and property circumstances; this mortgage estimate does not calculate those taxes.
rules: MAS macroprudential settings list housing-loan LTV limits of 75% for a first housing loan, 45% for a second and 35% for a third; tighter limits can apply for longer tenures or loans extending beyond retirement age.

MAS sets a 55% Total Debt Servicing Ratio cap and a 30% Mortgage Servicing Ratio cap for specified HDB-flat and executive-condominium loans. These are regulatory frameworks, not a guarantee of individual approval.
IRAS Buyer's Stamp Duty is based on the higher of purchase price or market value; Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty may also apply. The calculator does not calculate these taxes.
sources: IRAS: Stamp duty rates and taxes

BR.summary: Brazilian residential property finance distinguishes the SFH (Housing Finance System) and SFI (Real Estate Financing System). Conditions, eligibility and cost structures differ; banks assess the borrower's repayment capacity.
rules: The Central Bank of Brazil explains the SFH and SFI financing systems and their different eligibility and property conditions.
Lenders assess income and existing financial commitments; the Central Bank FAQ notes that each bank applies its own income-commitment criteria.
The calculator does not determine SFH/SFI eligibility, FGTS eligibility, effective total cost (CET), property registration or local transfer taxes.
sources: Banco Central do Brasil: Real-estate credit FAQ
Banco Central do Brasil: Conditions for real-estate financing

ZA.summary: South Africa's National Credit Act provides consumer protections for mortgage agreements, including a pre-agreement statement and quotation before signing. These documents should set out the deposit, instalments, interest and charges.
rules: Request and review the pre-agreement statement and quotation before signing a mortgage agreement.
The National Credit Regulator's consumer guidance says the quotation should disclose the principal debt, interest rate, total amount payable, instalments, fees, charges and interest.
This calculator does not apply bank-specific affordability tests, transfer duty, bond registration costs or credit-life insurance.
sources: National Credit Regulator: Consumer rights under the National Credit Act
National Credit Regulator: National Credit Act brochure

SA.summary: Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) rules require mortgage providers to assess a borrower's ability to repay and prudently value the property when calculating loan-to-value. LTV treatment can vary by first-home status, beneficiary and finance-provider type.
rules: SAMA's real-estate finance rulebook requires underwriting policies to assess ability to repay and sets out how LTV and property value are calculated.
SAMA has issued different LTV treatment for citizens' first homes and for subsequent homes, with differences between banks and real-estate finance companies. Do not treat one percentage as universal.
The calculator does not test Sharia-compliant product structure, debt-burden limits, borrower eligibility or SAMA's detailed LTV categories.
sources: SAMA Rulebook: Real estate exposure class
SAMA Rulebook: Increase the maximum mortgage for citizens' first home

MX.summary: Mexico's CONDUSEF advises consumers to assess their ability to pay and compare mortgage offers, including the binding offer, commissions, limitations and final credit conditions. It also provides an official mortgage comparison simulator.
rules: CONDUSEF recommends checking real payment capacity and comparing bank mortgage conditions before signing.
Ask for the oferta vinculante (binding offer) and compare the amount financed after commissions, exclusions and product limitations.
The calculator does not model Infonavit/Fovissste programmes, Mexican CAT (total annual cost), notary costs, local acquisition taxes or lender-specific terms.

JP.summary: Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism publishes official housing-tax guidance, including the housing-loan tax deduction. Eligibility and deduction limits depend on the tax year, occupancy date, property type and energy-performance conditions.
rules: Check the MLIT housing-tax guidance for the applicable year before estimating a housing-loan tax deduction.
The tax deduction is separate from the mortgage repayment calculation; this calculator does not estimate income-tax relief or verify property eligibility.
The official source is primarily in Japanese; consult the current tax authority guidance or a qualified local adviser for your circumstances.
sources: MLIT Japan: Housing tax measures (2026 update)

MY.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) emphasizes responsible housing finance and affordability assessments. Banks determine individual lending decisions; a single universal down-payment or LTV percentage should not be assumed.
rules: BNM says financial institutions assess income after statutory deductions, essential expenditure and other obligations to ensure borrowers can afford repayments and retain a financial buffer.
BNM states that it does not prescribe one universal housing-loan lending limit; banks make lending decisions under their own criteria and risk appetite.
Floating-rate housing-loan instalments may change when the Overnight Policy Rate changes; confirm the reference rate and reset terms with the lender.
sources: BNM: First-time home owners continue to have access to financing
BNM: Responsible lending and borrower affordability
BNM: How monetary policy affects floating-rate housing loans

ID.summary: Bank Indonesia's October 2026 policy report extends a temporary 100% LTV/FTV ceiling for property financing from 1 January through 31 December 2027, but only at banks meeting specified non-performing loan/financing criteria. This is a conditional macroprudential ceiling, not a borrower's entitlement or a promise of full-value financing.
rules: The temporary 100% LTV/FTV ceiling applies to property financing at banks meeting specified NPL/NPF criteria and is extended for contracts from 1 January to 31 December 2027.
A 100% regulatory ceiling does not mean a lender must finance the full purchase price; the lender still applies its own underwriting, valuation and borrower assessment.
The calculator does not include Indonesian BPHTB, notary/PPAT, insurance, administrative fees, subsidy eligibility or bank-specific requirements.
sources: Bank Indonesia: Monetary Policy Report — Quarter III 2026 (property LTV/FTV extension)

KR.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission announced a 2026 household-debt plan that includes regional and borrower-category-specific mortgage restrictions. Rules vary by location, property, loan purpose and lender type; the calculator does not determine eligibility.
rules: The Financial Services Commission's 2026 plan continues quantitative management of household debt and adds separate management targets for home-mortgage lending.
Some restrictions apply specifically to multi-home owners and apartment mortgages in the Seoul metropolitan and speculation-regulated areas; exemptions and transition rules may apply.

For online P2P mortgage loans, from 2 April 2026 the FSC specifies LTV limits of 40% in Seoul metropolitan/speculation-regulated areas and 70% in non-regulated areas, with additional property-value loan caps. These are not universal bank-mortgage limits.

Confirm the current FSC/FSS rules and lender assessment for the property's exact location and the borrower's circumstances. The calculator does not calculate Korean acquisition tax, registration costs or policy-loan eligibility.
sources: Financial Services Commission: Government Unveils 2026 Household Debt Management Plan (1 April 2026)

TH.summary: The Bank of Thailand announced a temporary relaxation of residential-mortgage LTV ceilings for contracts made from 1 July 2026 through 30 June 2027. The 100% ceiling applies only to specified property-price and loan-sequence categories and does not guarantee lender approval.
rules: For contracts signed from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027, the temporary 100% LTV ceiling applies to homes valued below THB 10 million from the second housing-loan contract onward, and homes valued at THB 10 million or more from the first contract onward.
This is a temporary regulatory ceiling, not a requirement that banks lend 100% or an assurance that a borrower qualifies; lenders still assess credit risk and repayment capacity.
The calculator does not include Thai transfer and mortgage registration fees, taxes, insurance, lender charges or other borrower-specific conditions.
sources: Bank of Thailand: Extension of temporary LTV relaxation through 30 June 2027 (14 May 2026)
Bank of Thailand: Mortgage loan consumer explanation

PH.summary: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas prudential rules distinguish bank-level real-estate exposure limits from an individual household's mortgage eligibility. The residential loans of individual households for owner-occupied housing are treated separately from the aggregate bank portfolio cap; this is not an individual LTV allowance.
rules: BSP's Manual of Regulations for Banks sets a prudential limit on certain banks' aggregate real-estate loan exposures, while excluding specified loans to individual households for acquisition, construction or improvement of housing they will occupy.

That portfolio-level exclusion must not be interpreted as a guaranteed individual loan amount, deposit percentage or LTV limit. Banks apply their own underwriting and applicable consumer-credit rules.
The calculator does not include Philippine documentary stamp tax, local transfer tax, registration fees, mortgage redemption insurance, Pag-IBIG eligibility or lender-specific charges.
sources: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas: Manual of Regulations for Banks — Part III, Loans and Credits, Section 363-A

AR.summary: Argentina's official housing-finance information describes UVA-denominated mortgage loans, where the unit is updated daily by the CER index, and the national government provides information about eligible housing purposes. BCRA's transparency regime publishes lender-reported mortgage product terms for comparison; rates and conditions vary by institution and must be checked at the time of application.
rules: UVA is an inflation-indexed unit whose value is updated daily using CER; a UVA-denominated loan balance and payments expressed in pesos can therefore change as the unit value changes.

Official government information describes eligible purposes for certain UVA housing loans, including purchase, replacement, construction, expansion, renovation and completion of a single permanent residence, subject to each programme's terms.

BCRA's financial-product transparency regime publishes lender-reported mortgage loan terms and comparison data. Check the latest lender-specific data and the actual loan contract; published product terms are not a universal approval promise.
The calculator does not estimate UVA/CER indexation, programme eligibility, provincial or municipal taxes, notary/registry costs, insurance or lender-specific charges.
sources: Argentina Government: How to access a UVA mortgage loan

CL.summary: Chile's Financial Market Commission (CMF) explains mortgage affordability, lender underwriting, loan-rate types and its official mortgage comparison simulator. Lenders set their own approval conditions; CMF's educational material notes that some institutions recommend a dividend near 25% of income as a guideline, not a universal statutory ceiling.
rules: Assess the proposed mortgage payment together with existing household expenses and other debts; leave room for unexpected expenses.

CMF educational material says several institutions recommend the future mortgage dividend be at most around 25% of total applicant income (or combined income with a guarantor). This is an institution-level rule of thumb, not a universal legal LTV or eligibility threshold.
Mortgage rates may be fixed, variable or mixed; compare the rate type, payment changes, fees and insurance as well as the headline rate.

Lenders independently assess income, employment, credit information and property documentation. The CMF mortgage simulator can help compare published offers, but the calculator does not include Chilean UF index movements, stamp duties, registration costs, insurance or lender-specific conditions.
sources: CMF Educa: How to obtain a mortgage loan

CO.summary: Colombia's Law 546 of 1999 sets a specialised framework for long-term individual housing finance. It provides for UVR-denominated loans and permits peso-denominated alternatives under specified fixed-rate and amortisation conditions. The law requires lender assessment of borrower and collateral capacity; these provisions are not a promise of approval.
rules: Long-term individual housing loans under Law 546 may be denominated in UVR; peso-denominated loans are also permitted when the statutory conditions are met, including a fixed interest rate for the full loan term and no interest capitalisation.
The law specifies a minimum amortisation term of five years and a maximum term of at least thirty years as set by the government; confirm current implementing rules and the individual lender's offer.
The law provides for full or partial prepayment without penalty for qualifying long-term housing loans, subject to the statutory framework.

Lenders must assess information about the borrower and the collateral to evaluate repayment capacity and security. The calculator does not estimate UVR indexation, housing subsidy eligibility, taxes, notary/registration costs, insurance or bank-specific fees.
sources: Colombia: Law 546 of 1999 — official legal text
Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia: Housing loan consumer guide
Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia: Housing loan FAQs

CN.summary: China's National Financial Regulatory Administration and People's Bank of China issued the 2026 trial Measures for Administration of Individual Housing Loans. They require lender assessment of identity, creditworthiness, repayment capacity, down-payment ability and acceptable security. The maximum loan term is 40 years; minimum down-payment policy is set by the authorities and lenders may set higher levels based on local market, project and borrower risk.
rules: Under the 2026 trial measures, eligible borrowers must have legal identification, good credit, willingness and ability to repay, capacity to pay the down payment and acceptable collateral.

The minimum down-payment ratio is determined by the People's Bank of China and the National Financial Regulatory Administration; lenders may set the actual ratio based on local property-market conditions, project characteristics, credit and repayment capacity. This page does not assume one national percentage.
The maximum individual housing-loan term is 40 years. Loans with a term over one year are repaid monthly under the trial measures.
Mortgage rates are agreed by borrower and lender subject to applicable national rules and self-regulatory requirements; lenders may use differentiated risk-based pricing.
The calculator does not include Chinese deed tax, VAT, personal income tax treatment, local purchase restrictions, provident-fund loan eligibility or bank-specific underwriting.
sources: NFRA and People's Bank of China: Trial Measures for Administration of Individual Housing Loans (28 August 2026)
NFRA: Trial Measures — borrower conditions and down-payment policy

EG.summary: Egypt's mortgage-finance framework is supervised by the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) under Mortgage Finance Law No. 148 of 2001, as amended. The Egyptian Mortgage Federation's consumer FAQ describes residential finance up to 90% of appraised/agreed value and monthly-installment-to-income thresholds that vary by borrower category; these are framework/product guidance and must be confirmed with the licensed financier and current programme terms.
rules: The Egyptian Mortgage Federation FAQ states a maximum residential mortgage-finance ratio of 90% of property value, based on the lower of the appraisal value or agreed sale price. This is federation consumer guidance, not a guarantee that every lender will offer 90%.

The same FAQ describes monthly instalment limits of 35% of monthly income for low-income borrowers and 40% for specified social-housing and other borrowers. Confirm the current applicable programme, income definition and lender underwriting before relying on these figures.
The FAQ describes mortgage finance terms that may extend to 20 years or more, with certain low-income housing programmes extending up to 30 years subject to contract and programme rules.

Mortgage finance may involve administrative, application-study, valuation, insurance and guarantee costs. The calculator does not estimate Egyptian stamp/registration costs, subsidy eligibility, currency/inflation effects or lender-specific fees.
The FRA identifies Mortgage Finance Law No. 148 of 2001 as part of the laws it supervises. Use a licensed mortgage-finance provider and check current FRA rules.
sources: Egyptian Mortgage Federation: Mortgage-finance consumer FAQ
Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority: About FRA and laws under its supervision

NG.summary: Nigeria's National Housing Fund (NHF) is a specific government-backed housing-finance scheme administered through accredited mortgage loan originators; its eligibility rules should not be confused with the terms of every commercial mortgage. The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria's published conditions require NHF contributions, documented regular income and residential-purpose use, with the property serving as security.
rules: For the NHF scheme, FMBN's published conditions say applicants must be Nigerian and at least 18 years old, have contributed to the National Housing Fund for at least six months, and show a regular income flow sufficient to support repayment.
NHF financing is for building, purchasing or renovating residential accommodation; applicants apply through an accredited mortgage loan originator, not directly to FMBN.
The property is used as security and must comply with planning requirements, have adequate value and be insured against hazards.

FHA Mortgage Bank's published NHF product information describes a maximum repayment period of 30 years and an affordability test using about one-third of applicant income. These are scheme/product terms and must be checked against the current offer and eligibility rules.

Do not apply the NHF terms as universal limits for all Nigerian mortgages. The calculator does not determine NHF contribution history, scheme allocation, title validity, fees, insurance, state registration charges or lender-specific credit approval.
sources: Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria: Conditions for NHF Loan (official PDF)
FHA Mortgage Bank: NHF loan product and eligibility
Nigeria Mortgage Refinance Company: Uniform Underwriting Standards overview

AF.summary: Da Afghanistan Bank (DAB) publishes the Law on Mortgage of Immovable Property and supervises the banking and credit-registration framework. DAB's credit registry gathers borrower and guarantor information from banks and microfinance institutions to support credit-risk decisions. The public DAB material reviewed does not establish one nationwide retail mortgage loan-to-value ceiling, borrower debt-service cap or standard repayment term; terms must be confirmed with a licensed lender and checked against applicable property and mortgage law.
rules: DAB lists the Law on Mortgage of Immovable Property among Afghanistan's banking and financial laws. Confirm that the property title, mortgage documentation, registration and enforcement process comply with the applicable law before relying on a financing estimate.

DAB's Public Credit Registration System collects borrower identification, background and guarantee information from commercial banks and participating microfinance institutions and supplies credit reports to relevant financial institutions.

DAB also describes an electronic register for mortgages of movable property used in banking transactions. DAB clarifies that this movable-property register does not create or transfer real-estate ownership rights; do not confuse it with registration of a mortgage over a home.

The DAB sources reviewed do not establish a universal residential mortgage LTV ratio, debt-service-to-income cap or standard maximum term. Lender-specific underwriting, collateral valuation, income evidence, fees and repayment terms must be confirmed directly.
This calculator does not assess local title validity, legal enforceability, lender availability, currency or exchange-rate risk, or any bank's credit decision.
sources: Da Afghanistan Bank: Laws — includes Law of Mortgage on Immovable Property
Da Afghanistan Bank: Public Credit Registration and Financial Services Development

AL.summary: The Bank of Albania regulates consumer and mortgage credit. Its amended Regulation 48/2015, effective 12 February 2025, sets pre-contractual and contractual disclosure and conduct standards. In May 2025 the Supervisory Council approved upper limits for residential mortgage loan-to-value (LTV) and debt-service-to-income (DSTI), differentiated by property type and loan currency. The public announcement does not state the numeric ceilings, so this calculator does not invent a single national percentage.
rules: Banks and licensed non-bank financial institutions are subject to the Bank of Albania's Regulation 48/2015 on consumer and mortgage credit, which sets standards for pre-contractual and contractual information and the arrangement of mortgage credit.
The amended Regulation 48/2015 entered into force on 12 February 2025; the Bank of Albania notes that Article 15/1 requirements entered into force on 1 May 2025.

On 7 May 2025, the Bank of Albania announced upper limits for LTV and debt-service-to-income on residential real-estate loans. The limits are differentiated according to property type and loan currency; the announcement does not publish the numerical ceilings, so confirm the applicable limit with the lender and current regulation.

Compare the lender's effective borrowing cost, interest-rate reset terms, fees, required own contribution, collateral valuation and early-repayment conditions. Bank product terms may differ and are not universal national rules.
The calculator does not assess Albanian credit eligibility, property-title status, notary/registration costs, taxes or the applicable LTV/DSTI ceiling for an individual loan.
sources: Bank of Albania: Regulation 48/2015 on consumer credit and mortgage credit (integrated version)
Bank of Albania: Supervisory Council decisions, 7 May 2025 — residential mortgage LTV and DSTI limits

DZ.summary: Algerian home-finance terms are product- and lender-specific. Official bank products published by Crédit Populaire d'Algérie (CPA) and Banque de Développement Local (BDL) describe financing that can reach 90% for specified products, subject to borrower capacity and eligibility; CPA's particular product describes a possible term up to 40 years, while BDL describes up to 35 years. These are individual bank-product terms, not a universal national entitlement or LTV rule. Bank of Algeria prudential capital rules must not be mistaken for borrower-facing down-payment limits.
rules: CPA's published product for purchasing a home from a private individual describes financing up to 90% of the purchase price, generally at least 10% own contribution, and repayment up to 40 years subject to applicant age and repayment capacity. It also describes a possible own-contribution waiver for qualifying applicants under 40, subject to debt capacity. These are terms of that specific CPA product, not a rule for every Algerian lender.

BDL's real-estate loan page describes financing up to 90% and monthly repayment up to 35 years for eligible individuals with regular income. The amount granted depends on income and age and the selected product.

CPA's published product requires a stable and regular income, legal capacity and a first-ranking notarised mortgage; it also describes monthly instalments, insurance and fees. Confirm current product terms and charges with the lender before using any percentage or term.

Bank of Algeria Regulation 2014-01 includes an 80% property-value condition for a preferential regulatory risk-weight treatment of certain residential mortgage exposures. This is a bank capital-risk classification condition, not a universal borrower LTV cap or a promise of 80% financing.
The calculator does not determine eligibility for CPA/BDL products, Islamic finance terms, property-title validity, notarial and registration costs, insurance, subsidies or bank-specific approval.
sources: Crédit Populaire d'Algérie: Real-estate loan for purchase from a private individual
Banque de Développement Local: Real-estate loan
Bank of Algeria: Regulation 2014-01 — prudential risk weighting for residential real-estate loans

AD.summary: Andorra has a Government-backed first-home ownership programme for eligible residents, alongside ordinary bank mortgage products. Under the programme, the Government guarantees the mortgage during the initial seven years and pays the interest during that period; the beneficiary's payment is directed to principal. From year eight, the published rate is variable at 12-month Euribor plus a maximum 0.50%. The programme is conditional and should not be confused with standard market mortgages.
rules: The Government's first-home programme is for habitual and permanent residence. Published eligibility includes at least seven years of legal, effective and permanent residence, no home owned in Andorra or abroad, assets below 30% of the home's price and a maximum purchase price of €600,000. Confirm the current call and full eligibility conditions before applying.
For approved programme loans, the Government guarantees 100% of the loan during the first seven years and pays interest during that period; the beneficiary's instalment is used to repay principal.

The Government's current programme page describes a monthly instalment equivalent to 33% of beneficiary income, a 12-month Euribor + 0.50% maximum variable rate from year eight, and a 20-to-50-year repayment term, subject to the borrower not exceeding age 80 at maturity.

Programme approval requires a positive bank solvency assessment and subsequent review by the National Housing Institute and relevant public authorities. Government guarantee is not automatic mortgage approval.

The calculator does not test Andorran programme eligibility, guarantee availability, tax or notarial costs, foreign-purchase restrictions, or individual bank underwriting. Standard bank mortgage conditions may differ.
sources: Government of Andorra: First-home ownership access programme
Government of Andorra: Programme eligibility and current operating details
Andorran Financial Authority: Specialised credit entities and mortgage-credit activity under Law 7/2013

AO.summary: Angola's Banco Nacional de Angola (BNA) Notice No. 09/2024 establishes a special housing-credit regime. Banco BIC's published description of the BNA scheme states a 7% annual nominal rate for eligible housing loans up to Kz 150 million and restricts the first modality to homes built after 2012. These are special-scheme conditions, not universal terms for all Angolan mortgages; the lender must assess repayment capacity and property risk.
rules: Banco BIC describes its housing-credit product under BNA Notice No. 09/2024 as a special scheme for eligible residential properties built after 2012, with a 7% annual nominal rate for loans up to Kz 150 million. Confirm current availability, eligible property types and the applicable legal text with the bank before relying on these terms.
The special scheme is distinct from ordinary bank mortgage products. Do not assume the 7% rate, financing ceiling or eligibility applies to every bank, every property or every borrower.

BNA scheme information requires a careful assessment of the customer's financial capacity and property/project risks; banks may apply internal credit-risk rules and request valuation, legal title and supporting documents.
Budget separately for property valuation, notarial and registration formalities, insurance and applicable taxes or commissions; these may not be included in the repayment estimate.
This calculator does not determine eligibility for the BNA special scheme, validate Angolan land/property registration, calculate local taxes or fees, or predict lender approval.
sources: Banco BIC: Special housing and construction credit regime under BNA Notice No. 09/2024
Banco Nacional de Angola: Official website and banking regulation portal
RegAlert: Full text summary of BNA Notice No. 09/2024 (secondary legal text reference)

AG.summary: Antigua and Barbuda mortgage terms are lender- and product-specific. Eastern Caribbean Amalgamated Bank (ECAB) publicly describes mortgage products with financing up to 90% and terms up to 30 years; its construction product may finance construction costs where land is already owned. These are ECAB product terms, not a national statutory LTV or guaranteed borrower entitlement. The Eastern Caribbean Home Mortgage Bank (ECHMB) supports regulated primary lenders and does not lend directly to individual homebuyers.
rules: ECAB's published mortgage product describes financing up to 90% and a maximum term of 30 years. Higher financing may depend on lender criteria and mortgage indemnity insurance; the published terms are specific to ECAB and can change.

ECAB describes 100% financing of construction costs where the applicant already owns the land, subject to its lending criteria and property/security requirements. This is not a universal national rule.

ECAB's application guidance identifies income/employment evidence, bank references, property valuation and assigned property and life insurance as possible requirements. Confirm the current checklist, interest rate, fees and early-repayment conditions directly with the lender.
ECHMB provides mortgage funding to regulated primary lenders in the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union; it states that homebuyers should apply to a regulated primary lender, not directly to ECHMB.

The ECCB Office of Financial Conduct supervises market conduct for licensed financial institutions in the ECCU and provides a consumer complaint process. This calculator does not establish lender eligibility, local land-title status, legal fees, insurance costs or property taxes.
sources: Eastern Caribbean Amalgamated Bank: Mortgage loans
Eastern Caribbean Home Mortgage Bank: Mortgage credit facility and approved primary lenders
Eastern Caribbean Home Mortgage Bank: Frequently asked questions — ECHMB does not lend directly to individuals
ECCB Office of Financial Conduct: Consumer conduct supervision and complaints

AM.summary: Armenia's Law on Home Mortgage (25 October 2017) regulates borrower and lender relations, disclosures and home-mortgage contracts. The Central Bank of Armenia also publishes minimum criteria for certain residential loans to receive preferential 50/75% risk-weight treatment; those prudential criteria should not be mistaken for a universal legal LTV or affordability ceiling for every mortgage. The National Mortgage Company publishes separate underwriting rules for participating financial institutions under its refinancing programmes.
rules: Armenia's Law on Home Mortgage regulates disclosure by mortgagees, formation of home-mortgage contracts and related consumer protections. Review the effective annual interest rate, all contract terms, fees, insurance and early-repayment provisions before signing.

The Central Bank's minimum criteria for certain mortgage loans to qualify for preferential risk-weight treatment include a loan amount not exceeding 70% of the lower of market value or purchase price, monthly mortgage payments not exceeding 40% of borrower income, and total regular loan payments not exceeding 50%. These are bank prudential risk-weight criteria for qualifying loans, not a universal statutory maximum for every mortgage.

The National Mortgage Company's published underwriting standards for participating financial institutions under its programmes specify a maximum total debt-to-income ratio of 45% in standard cases, with up to 60% for specified non-standard acquisition or construction loans. These programme rules are not necessarily the terms of every lender or loan.
Banks assess income, existing liabilities, property valuation and collateral; insurance and documentation requirements may apply. Confirm the exact product and programme rules with the lender.
The calculator does not establish Armenian mortgage eligibility, calculate state subsidy entitlement, verify property registration, or include notary, registration, insurance and lender fees.
sources: ARLIS: Law of the Republic of Armenia on Home Mortgage (25 October 2017)
Central Bank of Armenia: Regulation 2 — minimum requirements for mortgage loans with 50/75% risk weight
National Mortgage Company: Rules and regulations for participating financial institutions

AZ.summary: Azerbaijan's Mortgage and Credit Guarantee Fund (MCGF) publishes conditions for ordinary and preferential mortgage loans funded through the Fund. For these specific Fund-backed programmes, ordinary mortgages may finance up to 85% of appraised value and preferential mortgages up to 90%, with programme-specific maximum amounts, terms and interest-rate ceilings. These conditions do not describe every commercial mortgage product in Azerbaijan.
rules: For MCGF-funded mortgages, the official Fund page states a maximum loan-to-value of 85% for ordinary mortgages and 90% for preferential mortgages, corresponding to minimum own contributions of 15% and 10%, respectively.
The Fund lists maximum loan amounts of AZN 150,000 for ordinary mortgages and AZN 100,000 for preferential mortgages. Maximum terms are 25 years and 30 years, respectively.

The Fund lists maximum annual interest rates of 8% for ordinary and 4% for preferential unsecured loans, and 7% for ordinary and 3.7% for preferential secured loans. Confirm the current product and guarantee fee with the authorized bank and Fund.

The Fund states that monthly mortgage payments generally must not exceed 70% of the borrower's total monthly income, and the borrower must retain a minimum amount for family living expenses. Official income, independent property appraisal, state registration of the mortgage and property insurance are required under the Fund programme.

Eligibility for preferential mortgages is restricted to specified categories and the preferential benefit can generally be used once. The calculator does not determine category eligibility, guarantee approval, local purchase taxes, valuation costs or lender-specific fees.
sources: Mortgage and Credit Guarantee Fund of Azerbaijan: Mortgage loan terms and conditions
Mortgage and Credit Guarantee Fund of Azerbaijan: Guarantee mechanism and application stages

BS.summary: The Central Bank of The Bahamas issued revised residential mortgage lending guidance on 29 December 2023. It removed mortgage indemnity insurance as a Central Bank stipulation for borrowers to qualify for a reduced equity contribution; in the absence of insurance the baseline minimum down payment was 15%, while lenders may set lower requirements under their own risk frameworks. Personal lending, including residential mortgages, remains subject to a prudent total debt-service ratio limit of 50%.
rules: The Central Bank's 29 December 2023 guidance removed mortgage indemnity insurance as a required condition for qualifying for a reduced residential mortgage down payment. Where that insurance is not used, the baseline minimum equity contribution was 15%; lenders may set lower down-payment requirements under their internal borrower-risk frameworks.

The Central Bank directs lenders to keep a borrower's total debt-service ratio within a prudent 50% limit, subject to stated exceptions for certain debt restructurings or consolidations that do not increase outstanding obligations.

Lenders must continue to assess the loan-to-value ratio prudently against the appraised value of the property. The 60%, 80% and above-80% LTV bands cited in the Central Bank release determine bank capital risk weights; they are not individual borrower LTV entitlements or universal lending caps.
A lender may apply stricter underwriting, property valuation, insurance, income verification and down-payment requirements. Confirm the current policy and fees with the bank or credit union.
The calculator does not determine eligibility, mortgage indemnity insurance availability, property insurance, stamp duty, conveyancing, valuation or other Bahamian closing costs.
sources: Central Bank of The Bahamas: Relaxed Lending Rules for Residential Mortgages (29 December 2023)
Central Bank of The Bahamas: Official PDF of the 29 December 2023 mortgage guidance

BB.summary: Barbados has a Housing Credit Fund (HCF) administered through approved financial institutions for eligible low-income households, with published affordability and term limits. This programme is distinct from ordinary commercial bank and credit-union mortgages, whose underwriting and rates are set by individual lenders. The Central Bank's financial-stability reporting describes market lending practices but should not be treated as a universal statutory LTV or debt-service cap.
rules: Under the Central Bank of Barbados Housing Credit Fund programme, loan disbursements are based on an affordability formula that allows no more than one-third of the applicant household's gross income to service the loan.

The HCF programme sets a maximum mortgage maturity of 30 years and a maximum 15-year term for home-improvement loans. The approved financial institution applies its normal underwriting procedures and assesses income, qualification and property valuation.

The financial institution carries the full credit risk and may take the security it considers appropriate. The interest rate charged to the beneficiary is negotiated between the financial institution and the borrower; the Central Bank sets the HCF lending rate to approved institutions.

The HCF rules apply to beneficiaries of that programme, not automatically to every mortgage borrower in Barbados. The Central Bank's financial-stability reports describe observed market LTV and debt-service ratios; those observations are not universal borrower entitlements or legal caps.
The calculator does not test HCF eligibility, grant availability, bank-specific affordability, insurance, legal fees, valuation or property transfer costs.
sources: Central Bank of Barbados: Support for Households — Housing Credit Fund terms
Central Bank of Barbados: MoneySmart — preparing to apply for a mortgage
Central Bank of Barbados: 2025 Financial Stability Report

BY.summary: Belarus's National Bank Resolution No. 149 of 29 March 2018, as amended, establishes bank lending procedures and borrower disclosures. For natural persons, the instruction prohibits foreign-currency lending and requires banks to assess creditworthiness for real-estate financing using a loan-coverage ratio (LCR) based on the loan amount and collateral value. The reviewed National Bank instruction does not prescribe a single universal LTV percentage or standard mortgage term for all banks.
rules: Under the National Bank's Resolution No. 149 instruction, loans to natural persons in Belarus are provided in Belarusian roubles; foreign-currency loans to natural persons are not permitted.

When assessing a natural person's application for real-estate financing, the bank must apply a loan-coverage ratio (LCR), calculated using the loan amount and the value of the real estate accepted as collateral and/or other collateral under the agreement.

Banks must provide the borrower with written information on lending terms before signing a loan agreement or certain amendments. Review the interest rate, fees, repayment schedule, security and all other contract terms.

The instruction requires banks to set their own internal procedures for creditworthiness assessment, collateral valuation and loan decisions. Do not assume one universal LTV ceiling, interest rate or maximum mortgage term for all Belarusian lenders.

The calculator does not assess Belarusian housing-subsidy eligibility, state-supported housing programmes, property registration, currency conversion, legal costs, insurance or bank-specific credit approval.
sources: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus: Resolution No. 149 — Instruction on procedure of funds provision in the form of loans and repayment (amended)
National Bank of the Republic of Belarus: Financial stability report and mortgage-lending regulatory context
Republic of Belarus: Law No. 345-Z on Mortgage (20 June 2008, consolidated text)

BZ.summary: Belize distinguishes bank and credit-union lending from non-bank mortgage lending. The Financial Services Commission's legislation and licensing materials identify mortgage lending by non-bank persons as a regulated activity. The Development Finance Corporation (DFC) publishes housing-finance products for eligible applicants; its public FAQ lists a 10% client contribution for its Home Mortgage product, while separate DFC housing pathways may offer higher financing subject to repayment capacity, land/title, building approvals and collateral. These are DFC product conditions, not universal national mortgage limits.
rules: Belize's Financial Services Commission identifies mortgage lending by non-bank persons as a licensable financial-services activity. Verify that a non-bank mortgage provider holds the appropriate current licence; commercial banks and credit unions are governed under their respective legislation and supervisors.

DFC's published FAQ lists a 10% client contribution and 90% DFC contribution for its Home Mortgage product, with home-financing rates shown as a product range. Confirm the current rate, contribution, term and eligibility directly with DFC before relying on these figures.

DFC also describes specific housing-finance pathways that may provide up to 100% financing for qualifying applicants, depending on repayment capacity, land ownership or purchase, property documents and the intended construction or purchase plan. These special pathways should not be confused with the standard Home Mortgage product.

DFC may require title or lease documents, property-tax evidence, approved building plans and a bill of quantities for construction loans. Leasehold projects may require permission to mortgage from the Lands Department.
The calculator does not determine DFC programme eligibility, validate title or lease rights, calculate stamp duty, transfer tax, legal fees, insurance, valuation or local authority charges.
sources: Belize Financial Services Commission: Types of Licences — Mortgage Lending
Development Finance Corporation Belize: Home Loans
Development Finance Corporation Belize: Frequently Asked Questions — rates and client contribution
Belize Financial Services Commission Act No. 8 of 2023
